summary: A person STANDING IN FRONT OF A CAMERA was not detected, so face recognition wrote no alert, recorded no clip, sent no notification, and the roster never said 'last seen'. The feature looked switched on and did nothing, which is the worst way for a security feature to fail. SAME ROOT CAUSE AS THE PASSPORT PHOTO, at the other end of it: YuNet finds faces within a band of sizes RELATIVE to its input frame, and the live stage detected at the frame's NATIVE resolution. Measured against the shipped model on a 1920x1080 frame - the resolution a face rule forces - a face is found while it is roughly 7-20% of the frame height (somebody across the room) and NOT FOUND at 30%, 42% or 60% (somebody approaching, standing at the camera, or filling it). Every close-range framing, which is the entire point of a door camera and the first thing anybody tests, was invisible. THE FIX: detect on a 640-long copy first, then at native size, stopping at the first rung that finds a face, with rows mapped back to original coordinates either way so the crop and the faceprint still come from the full-resolution frame. The cheap rung runs first on purpose - measured here, 13ms against 88ms native - so the case that was broken is now the FASTEST one (a frame with somebody at the camera: 25ms, was 88ms and found nothing) while an empty frame pays both rungs, about 138ms against 88ms, on face-rule cameras only and once per sampling interval. Coverage goes from 7-20% to 7-74%. ALSO FIXED, the second half of the same failure: ONE decision - 'is this the enrolled person?' - was being made twice against different numbers. The worker attaches a name at cosine >= 0.40 and SFace's documented same-identity point is ~0.36, but infra/vision/face.go demanded 0.60, so every genuine match in between was named by the worker and thrown away here. Measured on one subject enrolled from a passport photo and seen on a 1080p camera, 2 of 7 ordinary views landed in that band (backlit at the camera 0.50, backlit across the room 0.59): on a 'known' rule they produced no alert at all, and on an 'unknown' rule they were WORSE THAN NOTHING - an enrolled person reported as a stranger. The default is now the worker's floor, 0.40. Proven through the worker's own live stage against the real gallery: a face at 150/320/450/650px in a 1080p frame is now found and NAMED at every distance, where the last three found nothing at all before. New infra/vision/face_test.go pins that this side is never stricter than the worker, covers all three match modes against the candidate shape the worker emits (including that an enrolled person must never fire an 'unknown' rule), and pins that a zone-less face rule covers the whole frame - the People screen creates them that way, and a zone-less rule that matched nothing would make every one of them silently inert. bench_face_enrol_framing.py now covers both stages: 12 framings, 5 uploads and 7 camera views.
compatibility: Backward-compatible; no API, schema or config change, and no restart needed beyond the usual detector reload. THE CONFIDENCE FLOOR IS A DELIBERATE LOOSENING and is stated as such: naming somebody is now accepted at cosine 0.40 instead of 0.60, which is the model's own same-identity range and the floor the worker already applied before attaching any name - but a lower floor does mean a higher chance of naming the WRONG person, and a site that wants the old strictness sets minConfidence: 0.6 on the rule, which the camera's AI rules editor now exposes. Existing rules that already carry an explicit minConfidence are unaffected. The live detection change costs more CPU on an EMPTY frame (both rungs run) and less on a frame with a face; it applies only to cameras with a face rule, once per vision sampling interval. Enrolled faceprints remain valid: what changed is which frames yield a candidate and which candidates count as recognized, not how a face is aligned or embedded.
